title: PageApiV1dot1
description: K-21 v1.1, a minor version for journey 3's screens (T-060; 02-contracts K-21 'Minor versions': customer screen 1 with journey 3, and the public listing page, FS section 6.3, with journey 3; section 9 F15). It only adds to v1 (page-api.v1.schema.json, frozen by T-030 and unchanged, referred to here): every v1 definition is here under its own name, all but callName by reference (callName takes only the four new names), so every v1 exchange is a v1.1 exchange. Added: the public page envelope (publicPage: the listing code, which names a business and one of its kinds of work, with no session and no link), the page entry's swap of card numbers and Social Security numbers in typed words (pageWordsSwap, with the named rule scrubbedPassedOn in page-api.rules.mjs) and four calls: readListing (one of the business's public listings, one per kind of work: S1-04, FS 6.3, which the booking page's screen 1 also shows: A3-04, B3-07; page-only, since no K-09 v1.1 call reads it), startBookingRequest (the booking page's first words: the live check, then K-09 v1.1 recordSafetyOutcome alone, source page, then K-09 v1.1 openRequest at door page, which gives request), bookingCheckStart (A3-43's and B3-35's tap on the booking page: K-09 v1.1 checkBookingFirst) and bookingCheckCode (the code typed back on the page: K-09 v1 proveCode once a K-09 minor version gives the page server the code id; until then the page entry checks no code and never answers checked, a code that does not match taking the no-match path: README default 29, open gap 34). A request still never names the person or the business it acts for: these pages act for no one, and the business is the one the listing code names, live only and only while the kind of work the code names is live too (publicPage). contracts/page-api/README.md, section 'v1.1', states for each call who may call it, how it is bound, what serves it, its repeat rule and its errors. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

callName.title: PageCallName
callName.description: Every call v1.1 holds: v1's (page-api.v1.schema.json callName, unchanged) and the four v1.1 adds (readListing, startBookingRequest, bookingCheckStart, bookingCheckCode); the only v1 definition v1.1 changes, and only by new enum values. Each has <call>.request, <call>.response, <call>.errors and <call>.exchange under $defs (02-contracts section 2 item 2). None of the four is staging-only (stagingOnlyCall is v1's, unchanged).

listingCode.title: ListingCode
listingCode.description: The code in the address of one of a business's public listings and its booking page (FS section 6.3; customer screen 1, FS section 7; A3-04: 'linked from its Google listing, its texts or a link Sam shared'). A company is listed under each of its kinds of work (S1-04: 'One company is one business, listed under each of its kinds of work. Each listing shows only its own licenses and people'; FS row B10: 'listing page (one listing per kind)'), so the code names the business and the kind (README defaults 24 and 40). No frozen part stores a listing or booking-page address (K-23 v1 default 4; Q-51: the host is a config value, rosfield.com/test on staging: DL-014, DL-023), so the address is the host plus /b/ plus the business part, a slash and the kind part. It is public, never a secret: it names which listing, never who is at the browser, and grants nothing a stranger could not do by text (A3-01: 'Every way in gets the same rules'). A code is live only when its business is live and its kind of work is live too, since each kind goes live on its own (S1-38: 'Each goes live on its own'; S1-50; README default 37). An unknown business, a business that is not live, a kind part that matches none of the business's kinds and a kind of work that is not live all get the same answer (notListed).

business.description: The business's own id (K-04 v1 businesses.id, an opaque id: CQ-09), as round 1's code was (README default 24).

kind.description: The kind part (README default 40): the first 16 characters of the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text '<business id>:<kind id>', where the kind id is one of the business's K-23 v1 company_kinds.kind_id (the profession file's id, such as barber or plumber: K-24 v1 kinds.id). A kind id is audience never and can name sensitive work (S13-22; FS row B02: a plain name in texts for sensitive work), so the address never spells it: the page entry works the code out for each of the business's kinds and takes the one that matches. The server makes only that form; the pattern admits other strings only so that a stale or mistyped code still gets notListed, as v1's linkCode does.

publicPage.title: PublicPageEnvelope
publicPage.description: What a request from a business's public page carries (v1.1: the public listing page and the booking page) in place of v1's page envelope: the page's own request id, the trace id and the listing code (the business and its kind of work). It carries no session token and no signed link: these pages act for no one (FS line 701: 'Customers have no login and no password'; S13-45: 'Opening a link never counts'; K-22 v1 rule 4), and no request names a person of its own. The action layer's page entry first checks that the code names a live business with that kind (K-04 v1 businesses.status live: S1-35; S1-32; K-23 v1 company_kinds) and that the kind itself is live, by K-09 v1 readSetup's per-kind rule (its readSetup.response kinds[].live for the business's pick of that kind: S1-38, 'Each goes live on its own'; S1-50, 'Plumbing · Now ... Electrical · Once you say yes'; S1-29 and S1-31, a kind kept offline, saved, while its agreement is unsigned; K-24 v1 kinds.source new_work, offline until Rosie's team approves its draft), which the page entry applies itself and shows nothing of; else it answers notListed having read and written nothing more (README default 37). Then it turns the envelope into K-09 v1.1's businessCaller: kind page, businessId the business the code names, personId null, traceId as given, and for each K-09 call a requestId of its own, as requestId below says.

requestId.description: The page's own id for this submit, made once per form by the web app and never reused: the key a repeat is known by, within the device token it came with (startBookingRequest, bookingCheckStart, bookingCheckCode), so the same id from another browser never matches (02-contracts section 2 item 2). How it reaches K-09 (said here once for every v1.1 call): it is never passed on as given; each K-09 call the page entry makes for the request (recordSafetyOutcome, openRequest, checkBookingFirst) carries a caller.requestId of its own, which the page entry makes and keeps on the server with this id and the device token's sha256, so a repeat of this request sends each K-09 call again under the same caller.requestId and gets its first result (K-09 repeated).

traceId.description: The trace the request opens (CQ-06: a page request opens its own trace id); each call adds its pageRequest span (K-08 v1) and passes the id on as K-09 caller.traceId.

notListedError.title: NotListedError
notListedError.description: The code names no public listing: no business has its business part, its business is not live (K-04 v1 businesses.status: S1-35 gives live; FS section 6.1: 'Nothing goes live until the ID, the control proof and the owner's OK to the fee are in', S1-32; B3-01 needs live), its kind part matches none of the business's kinds of work (K-23 v1 company_kinds; README default 40), or the kind it matches is not live (K-09 v1 readSetup's per-kind rule, kinds[].live: S1-38, 'Each goes live on its own'; S1-50; S1-29, S1-31; K-24 v1 new_work kinds offline until approved; README default 37). One answer for all four, so a code learns nothing (as v1's linkExpired). This check comes first (README default 37): nothing else was read and nothing was written, no safety read and no safety record included.

cannotBookHereError.title: CannotBookHereError
cannotBookHereError.description: The business can't take this request, with no reason given (S11-62's words toward a customer's own ways: 'AI assistants hear that the business can't take their booking, with no reason given'): the safety read holds a threat to staff or others, so nothing books, and the writer gets no safety message unless they are in crisis too, when safetyFirst's crisis line comes instead (A3-48: 'Someone who threatens others gets no safety message, unless they're in crisis too'; arch 06 line 325). The owner is told through recordSafetyOutcome's own rows (arch 06 line 329), never through this answer (README default 45).

notTakingNewBookingsError.title: NotTakingNewBookingsError
notTakingNewBookingsError.description: The owner has paused new bookings (K-23 v1 new_booking_pauses: an open row for this business; S11-15: 'While open, AI assistants and the booking page hear only "not taking new bookings"'). Nothing was written. Times already saved can still be confirmed (S11-15), which is journey 4's (K-21 v1.2). The page entry reads the pause itself, since K-09 v1.1 openRequest names no answer for it (README default 36; open gap 28).

safetyFirstError.title: SafetyFirstError
safetyFirstError.description: v1's answer for danger in a page's free words (answerOnPage's safetyFirst: the outcome row, the checked line's fixed line id and its words as the pinned bundle holds them), reused unchanged: the safety message comes back to the page and nothing books (arch 02 line 129: 'Danger returns the safety message to the caller, and nothing books'; A3-22, A3-24, A3-25, A3-48; B3-17; K-09 v1.1 recordSafetyOutcome, called alone with source page, whose safetyLine names the line). On the booking page it is also the answer, for now, to every outcome that lets a booking go on after its line (README default 37: until a K-09 minor version lets openRequest go on after a line, open gap 32), and to words the business's plug-in says stop a booking, with the business's own line (README default 44; open gap 33), so neither can ever quietly book.

goOnSafetyLine.title: GoOnSafetyLine
goOnSafetyLine.description: The checked line an opened request carries, for an outcome that lets the booking go on after its line (A3-22's branches that rejoin: 'Safety steps, then go on', A3-23: 'the plug-in's safety steps come first. Then the booking goes on, marked urgent'; 'Harm to a child or older adult', A3-49: 'If they came to book help for it, the booking goes on'; 'Unsafe at home', A3-50: 'If they want to go on, the booking becomes private from here'; 'Needs the business's own line', A3-26: 'Then the booking can go on', unless the plug-in's stop words block it; B3-18, B3-21; arch 06 line 319): the line's fixed line id and its words as the pinned bundle holds them (K-09 v1.1 recordSafetyOutcome.response.safetyLine, outboxRowId null for a page, which shows it: 'the caller is a page or an agent, which shows it'). Never a danger line: an emergency, crisis words and an unsure read never open a request (A3-24, A3-25; arch 06 line 323), and a threat gets no line (A3-48), so the line is never safetyEmergency, safetyCrisis or safetyAsk (K-01 v1 fixed lines; invalid/refuse-opened-after-emergency.json). The outcome itself is not sent: the page shows only the line.

fixedLineId.description: The line's id in the pinned bundle (K-09 v1 fixedLineId), never one of the danger lines.

words.description: The line's words as the pinned bundle holds them, with the business's slots filled (A3-26: the number Sam set for this line), word for word (arch 07 line 361).

pageWordsSwap.title: PageWordsSwap
pageWordsSwap.description: The page entry's swap (README default 39), stated as its own shape so a named rule can check it, as K-06 states the gateway's: one field of a page request that carries a person's typed words, as the browser sent it and as the page entry passes it on. Sources: arch 02 line 109 ('Before any write it swaps card numbers (13 to 19 digits, Luhn) and Social Security numbers for a tag'); arch 02 line 133 (Edge: 'card and SSN scrub before any write ... Secure pages and the agent API'); RULES lines 199 and 200 ('Never kept at all: full card numbers outside the card box, full Social Security numbers'). The page entry swaps first, before anything else reads the words: each card number and each Social Security number, read the wider way K-06 v1.1's scrubbedV1dot1 reads them (a 13 to 19 digit Luhn window in any run of digits, any run of spaces or dashes between groups, digits of any script), becomes its tag, '[card number]' or '[SSN]' (K-06 v1 README default 1's tags). Every later use holds the tag: the K-02 safety read, every K-09 call, the K-34 record of a read's evidence, every write and every later screen. The browser never sends this and no call answers it; its fixtures are the swap's own, checked by the named rule scrubbedPassedOn (page-api.rules.mjs).

call.description: The call whose request carries the field.

field.description: Where the field sits in that call's request, as a JSON pointer (RFC 6901), such as /words or /nameTyped.

typed.description: The field as the browser sent it. It lives only in the page entry's memory until the swap: never in a span, a log, an event-log row, a model call or any store.

passedOn.description: The field after the swap: what the safety read and every later use read. It holds no card number and no Social Security number, and differs from typed only where typed held one (scrubbedPassedOn).

localDate.title: LocalDate
localDate.description: A day in the business's zone, as YYYY-MM-DD (K-09 v1 localDate; CQ-05).

money.title: Money
money.description: An amount in whole cents with its currency code (CQ-09).

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: A three-letter currency code (CQ-09), the one money carries; named here as well, so the type generator resolves money's own reference to it.

listedPrice.title: ListedPrice
listedPrice.description: A way's price as the public pages show it (FS 6.3: 'Services with price kind and price (V01 to V04)'; A3-04: 'shows the same times and prices' an AI gets). words: the price in plain words the server builds (README default 30), such as '$35', '$120 an hour' or 'Quoted from your details'; amount: the list price of the K-25 v1 price rule in force at the read's moment for this service and way (the way's own rule where one names it, else the service's own: price_rules.service_money_id, price_cents and currency; effective dates: S11-54, README default 31), or null when the price is not a list price: known from photos or at the visit (FS row V02: the way's path's first part, K-25 v1 service_money.path) or set by the customer's answers (K-25 v1 services.price_kind by_answers). A price by worker or by time (T06; K-25 price_rules worker_resource_id, weekdays, from_time) shows on the times card, journey 4's (A4-14; open gap 31).

listedWay.title: ListedWay
listedWay.description: One way a service is offered (K-25 v1 service_money: one per service and place, FS line 725; S1-13, S1-43), with its price and its money rules beside it (FS 6.3: 'The money rules next to the first price: every charge the customer must pay, and the terms to cancel or miss', S11-57, S13-17).

place.description: Where it happens (K-25 v1 service_money.place; FS row L01): business, at the shop or office; customer, at the customer's place (flow B); meeting_spot; video (a video or phone visit, flow A).

locationId.description: K-25 v1 service_money.location_id: the shop, office or meeting spot (listing.locations); for place customer, the shop or office whose travel area a customer's address is checked against (L02, B4-77); null for video.

moneyLines.description: Every charge the customer must pay on this way and the terms to cancel or miss (FS 6.3 line 637: 'The money rules next to the first price: every charge the customer must pay, and the terms to cancel or miss'), in plain words the server builds (README default 30) only from columns whose audience names customers: the way's own row (K-25 v1 service_money: path, deposit_cents or deposit_percent, fee_cents, cutoff_before or cutoff_day_before_at), the business's flow default where the way sets no cutoff (K-23 v1 flow_defaults; H06), and for a way at the customer's place the travel fee for farther towns of the way's location (K-23 v1 locations.travel_fee_cents: FS row L03, 'price shown before the yes'; B4-77: 'If Sam set a travel fee for farther towns'), whose towns no source names (K-23 v1 open gaps), so the line says 'for farther towns' as the owner set it: what is taken when they book, what is paid after the visit, any travel fee, and the free-cancel time with the fee for a later cancel or a no-show (S11-57; S13-17; S13-55). Never the tip line (K-25 v1 service_money.tip_line is the owner's only) and never a word that holds money (RULES 3.2: never a hold).

listedLength.title: ListedLength
listedLength.description: A service's length as the public pages show it (FS 6.3: 'Services with price kind and price (V01 to V04)'; FS row V04: 'Length | minutes | R'), from K-25 v1 services.length (audience customer), which a booking holds: for one_price the whole service, for per_hour the shortest booking (such as event hours' 1-hour minimum), for per_unit and by_answers the time one unit takes, so a booking of several holds that many (README default 43).

words.description: The length in the server's plain words, by price kind (README default 43): one_price, the length itself, such as '30 minutes' or '2 hours 30 minutes'; per_hour, 'at least' and the length, such as 'at least 1 hour'; per_unit, the length 'each' and the unit, such as '1 day each night'; by_answers, the length 'each', such as '35 minutes each', since the answers set how many.

minutes.description: The same length in whole minutes (FS row V04's type), such as 30 or 150.

listedService.title: ListedService
listedService.description: One of the listing's services (A3-04: 'It lists only what Lee's Barbershop offers, with each service's price kind'; FS 6.3: V01 to V04): an active K-25 v1 services row of the listing's kind of work (services.kind_id: S1-04, 'Each listing shows only its own'; README default 41), in the owner's order (services.position: customers see the order, never the number), with its length and each active way.

serviceId.description: K-25 v1 services.id: the id the booking page's later screens name it by (K-21 v1.2).

name.description: K-25 v1 services.name (FS row V01), as the business set it.

priceKind.description: K-25 v1 services.price_kind (S1-12's four; FS rows V02, V03): one_price, per_hour, per_unit (with its unit) or by_answers (set by the customer's answers).

unit.description: K-25 v1 services.unit for per_unit, such as night; null otherwise.

length.description: The time it takes (FS row V04; K-25 v1 services.length), by price kind (listedLength).

listedLocation.title: ListedLocation
listedLocation.description: A shop, office or meeting spot of the business that one of the listing's ways names (K-23 v1 locations; FS rows B03, L01, L02; README default 41), with its hours (FS row H01). Not its kind: K-23 v1 locations.kind is the owner's only (audience owner); the page tells a meeting spot by its name.

locationId.description: K-23 v1 locations.id: a handle the listing's ways name it by, never shown (README default 42).

name.description: A meeting spot's name (K-23 v1 locations.name); null otherwise.

address.description: K-23 v1 locations.address (FS row B03 as the owner confirmed it): customers get the address (L02, B4-77), never its map point (K-23 v1 audience owner).

travelArea.description: Flow B's travel area from this location (FS row L02; K-23 v1 locations.travel_miles), or null when it has none. miles is K-23's numeric travel_miles rounded down to a whole mile, so the listing never shows an area wider than the owner set, and 1 when the stored value is under 1 (README default 33); the inside-or-outside answer at B4-77 uses the stored value. around is the location's own address when no other centre is set; when a centre other than the location's own is set (K-23 v1 travel_centre and travel_centre_address, audience owner: it may be the owner's home), around is null and the page shows the miles alone, with the inside-or-outside answer coming at B4-77 (K-23 v1 README open gaps; README default 33).

hours.description: The location's opening hours (FS row H01: K-27 v1 weekly_hours owned by the location, read in its own time zone), as plain lines the server builds, such as 'Mon to Fri, 9am to 5pm' (v1 default 22's rule); empty when none are set.

listedDocument.title: ListedDocument
listedDocument.description: A license, insurance or other document the business, a team member or a space gave and chose to show (K-35 v1 documents.shown_on_listing, not withdrawn; documents_listing_only_own_papers keeps a customer's and a booking's off; FS rows Q10, T08), for the listing's own kind of work only (S1-04: 'Each listing shows only its own licenses and people'; K-35 v1 documents.kind_id: README default 41), shown only as added by the business (FS 6.3: 'Licenses, insurance and other documents (Q10, T08) only as "added by the business". Never "checked", never a badge'; D96; MC C4, C7). Only its kind and its plain title (audience customer): never whose it is (K-35 v1 documents.owner_kind is the owner's only), never its number, issuer or end words (K-35 v1 documents.number, issuer and ends are sealed and stay so), never its file, and no field that says checked, verified or approved (README default 32).

documentId.description: K-35 v1 documents.id: a handle, never shown (README default 42).

kind.description: K-35 v1 documents.kind as stored (documents_kind_known), such as license or insurance.

title.description: K-35 v1 documents.title: what the paper is called, plain, such as 'Barber license'.

shownAs.description: Always addedByTheBusiness: the page shows it as 'added by the business' and nothing more (FS 6.3; D96).

listedPhoto.title: ListedPhoto
listedPhoto.description: One of the business's photos as the listing shows it (K-23 v1 business_photos, in the owner's order; FS row B07; S1-84): v1's shownPhoto (a short-lived signed address to read that one private file) with the photo's label, which the page uses as the image's text alternative (WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.1.1; T-793; the frontend engineer's note 1 on dc9295e).

photoId.description: K-23 v1 business_photos.id: a handle, never shown (README default 42).

url.description: A short-lived signed address to read this one private file (v1's shownPhoto.url; README 'Never in a span or a log').

expiresAt.description: When the signed address stops working (v1's shownPhoto.expiresAt).

label.description: K-23 v1 business_photos.label (audience customer; S1-84: '[photo: The shop front]'): a few words for what it shows, such as 'The shop front'; null when the owner gave none, and the page then says only that it is a photo of the business.

listedFaq.title: ListedFaq
listedFaq.description: One of the business's FAQs (K-23 v1 business_faqs, in the owner's order; FS row B08; S1-84).

readListing.request.title: ReadListingRequest
readListing.request.description: Read one of a business's public listings, the one for the kind of work its code names (FS section 6.3: 'What shows (S1-29 preview, S11-57 preview, A3-04)'; S1-04: 'One company is one business, listed under each of its kinds of work. Each listing shows only its own licenses and people'; FS rows B10, B01), which the booking page's screen 1 also shows (A3-04: 'It lists only what Lee's Barbershop offers, with each service's price kind. The page shows the business's About us line and photos (S1-84)'; FS section 7 screen 1; B3-07). Served by a page-only read of the action layer: no K-09 v1.1 call reads a business's public listing, and K-20's 'a business's details and services' (02-contracts K-20) is not frozen (T-029), so the page entry reads the rows itself (02-contracts K-21: 'each served by a Tool API call or a page-only call of the action layer'), under the business's own scope (arch 10 line 546): K-04 v1 businesses, K-23 v1 company_kinds, business_setup, business_photos, business_faqs, locations and new_booking_pauses, K-24 v1 kinds (the kind's name), K-25 v1 services, service_money and price_rules, K-27 v1 weekly_hours, K-22 v1 staff_skills (whose papers are the kind's: README default 41) and K-35 v1 documents. Every value it shows reads a column whose audience names customers (02-contracts section 2 item 3; RULES 4.5; README default 42: an opaque id is a handle and a currency code only writes an amount, neither shown). Its reads by business wait for K-05 v1.3 (open gap 35). Who may call: anyone with the page's address. Binds: the business and kind the code names, both live (publicPage; README default 37); the call acts for no one. Changes nothing: a read. Reads: the primary, uncached (arch 10 line 538: the replica serves search and reports only; the prices it shows are the ones a booking copies, RULES 3.7). Repeat: safe: a read. Time budget: none in the sources.

readListing.response.title: Listing
readListing.response.description: What one public listing shows (FS 6.3), for one kind of work of the business (README default 41): its trade name and the kind's name, its own services and only its own licenses and people (S1-04), with the business's display name, About us line, photos and FAQs, which K-23 v1 keeps per business, so each of its listings shows them. In the business's own words as stored and the server's plain words for lengths, prices and money rules (README defaults 30 and 43). No paid placement, no referral fee and no endorsement label: nothing here ranks or rates the business (FS 6.3; D99; S13-07). Reviews and ratings come from Rosie's own rating after a visit, with journey 10's version (A10-02), never for sensitive work (S13-22), so none is here (README default 34). A word the business's kinds ban (FS 6.3: 'Words a profession bans, like "licensed" for unlicensed work, never appear', S1-09, S13-11) is in no line: the server leaves out a stored line that holds one (README default 35). Never a map point, a travel centre other than the location's own address, a location's kind, whose a document is, its number, issuer or file, a tip line, or anything about a booking or a customer.

displayName.description: K-04 v1 businesses.display_name (FS row B02), or its name (B01) before B02 is set: the plain name customers see.

tradeName.description: The kind of work's own trade name (K-23 v1 company_kinds.trade_name, audience customer: S1-04, 'Each kind of work may keep its own trade name, like Lee Plumbing and Lee Electric'; FS row B01, 'a trade name per kind of work', shown on the listing page), or null when the kind keeps the business's own name, and the page shows displayName alone.

kindName.description: The name of the kind of work the listing is under (K-24 v1 kinds.name, audience customer, such as Barber or Plumber; S1-04: 'listed under each of its kinds of work').

about.description: The About us line (K-23 v1 business_setup.about; FS row B06), as the owner confirmed it at S1-84; null when there is none.

photos.description: The business's photos (K-23 v1 business_photos, in the owner's order; FS row B07; S1-84), each a short-lived signed address to read that one private file, with its label (listedPhoto).

services.description: The active services of the listing's kind of work only (K-25 v1 services.kind_id), in the owner's order (README default 41).

locations.description: The business's shops, offices and meeting spots that the listing's ways name (K-23 v1 locations; FS row L01: where each service happens), each once, in the order the services first name them, with their hours and travel areas (README default 41).

documents.description: The papers shown on the listing for its own kind of work only (README default 41), each only as added by the business.

newBookings.description: taking; or paused while the owner's PAUSE of new bookings holds (K-23 v1 new_booking_pauses, an open row; S11-15: the booking page hears only 'not taking new bookings'), when the booking page shows that line in place of its first question (README default 36).

readListing.exchange.title: ReadListingExchange
readListing.exchange.description: One readListing request with its outcome.

startBookingRequest.request.title: StartBookingRequestRequest
startBookingRequest.request.description: The booking page's first words (customer screen 1: 'asks what an AI would ask', FS section 7; A3-04 and B3-07: 'From here, the steps are the same as in an AI chat'), the request an AI would pass on (A3-02: 'the service and the day. No name, phone or street address yet'). Served by K-09 v1.1 recordSafetyOutcome, called alone with caller.kind page and source page (the words get the safety read before any answer the business gives: arch 02 line 129; A3-22, B3-17), then, when the read is No with nothing that blocks booking, K-09 v1.1 openRequest with door page (gives request: A3-01, B3-01; A3-04, B3-07), its flow set on the server (README default 38) and its booker a new person with no name (openRequest booker kind new), never a person the browser names. The page's own 'book' entry is A3-51's 'A new booking', as its safe default says (README default 25); A3-43's entry is bookingCheckStart. Order (README default 37): the page entry swaps card numbers and Social Security numbers in the words first, before anything reads them (pageWordsSwap; README default 39); then the code must name a live business with that kind of work, and that kind must be live too by K-09 v1 readSetup's per-kind rule (publicPage), else notListed, with no safety read and nothing written (the action-layer engineer's note c on dc9295e and FAIL 1 on e24ad04); then the safety read of the swapped words and its record under that business (an emergency, crisis words or an unsure read: safetyFirst, and nothing books; a threat to staff or others: cannotBookHere, with no line and no reason, and nothing books, A3-48 and README default 45; any other line, for now, also safetyFirst with nothing booked, until a K-09 minor version lets openRequest go on after a line, open gap 32; words the plug-in says stop a booking: safetyFirst with the business's own line, README default 44); then no open pause of new bookings (else notTakingNewBookings); then openRequest. Who may call: anyone with the booking page. Binds: the business from the code, it and the code's kind both live (publicPage); the call acts for no one (K-09 v1.1 businessCaller.personId null: 'an anonymous booking page'); the K-04 booking id and the booker's person id stay on the server with requestRef, bound to the device token, and never reach the browser (K-09 v1.1 open gap 29; README default 27). Changes: it opens a request in progress (the K-04 head at stage entry, the K-30 details row, the new person), which changes no booking, money or record of anyone's and is not read back on any way in (A3-01, A3-51; K-09 v1.1 openRequest); the customer's first change is read back and confirmed before the yes on screen 7's times card (FS section 7 screen 7: 'all before the yes'; A4-14; K-21 v1.2) (FS line 630; README default 26). Reads: the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe: page.requestId with the device token is the key; a repeat writes nothing and answers the same requestRef (K-09 v1.1 recordSafetyOutcome and openRequest answer repeated). Time budget: none in the sources; the safety read's own is 4 seconds (arch 02 line 111).

deviceToken.description: The browser's device cookie (v1's opaqueToken; v1 signInStart.deviceToken): the server keeps its sha256 with requestRef, so only this browser carries the request on (K-21 v1.2's screens).

words.description: The customer's words as typed. The page entry swaps every card number and Social Security number in them for its tag first, before anything reads them (pageWordsSwap; README default 39; arch 02 lines 109 and 133), and only the swapped words get the safety read (arch 02 line 129; K-02 v1 safety read, source page) and every later use. Neither form enters a span, a log or the event log; K-34 v1 keeps only the sealed evidence words a read names, from the swapped words (README 'Never in a span or a log', v1.1).

startBookingRequest.response.title: BookingRequestOpened
startBookingRequest.response.description: The request is open (K-09 v1.1 openRequest: gives request). The page goes on to the next screens, who it is for first (FS section 7 screen 2: A4-80, B4-92), which are K-21 v1.2's; they send requestRef back with the same device token.

requestRef.description: An opaque id the server makes for this request, never K-04's booking id or the booker's person id (K-09 v1.1 openRequest.response.bookingId and bookerPersonId stay on the server with it), with at least 128 bits from a cryptographically secure random generator, as v1's attempt ids (v1 default 18), bound on the server to the device token's sha256 and the business (README default 27).

safetyLine.description: The checked line the page shows first, for an outcome that lets the booking go on after its line (goOnSafetyLine; README default 37: 'Safety steps, then go on', A3-23; 'Harm to a child or older adult', A3-49; 'Unsafe at home', A3-50; 'Needs the business's own line' with no stop words, A3-26), or null when the read was No. Until a K-09 minor version lets openRequest go on after a line (open gap 32), K-09 v1.1 openRequest refuses every read but No, so the page entry answers each such line with safetyFirst and nothing books, and every opened answer has null here.

startBookingRequest.errors.title: StartBookingRequestErrors
startBookingRequest.errors.description: Nothing was booked. K-09 v1 recordSafetyOutcome's errors (tool-api.v1 recordSafetyOutcome.errors, unchanged in v1.1) map so: notFound gives notListed (a row the read names, the business, went away after the first check), bookingPaused gives bookingPaused and transient gives transient; nothing was recorded. K-09 v1.1 openRequest's answers map so: notLive gives notListed (the business went offline after the first check); bookingPaused gives bookingPaused; constraint and transient give transient; safetyHeld gives safetyFirst with the line recordSafetyOutcome named, or with the business's own line where it named none (README default 44), so a hold that blocks booking never quietly books. Its waitsForOwner, customerBlocked and notAllowed name a known person, phone or role, which a new person with no name and no handle never has, and its notFound a row this call never names.

startBookingRequest.exchange.title: StartBookingRequestExchange
startBookingRequest.exchange.description: One startBookingRequest request with its outcome.

bookingCheckStart.request.title: BookingCheckStartRequest
bookingCheckStart.request.description: A booking already made, checked first (A3-43, B3-35; S13-45's one rule), on the business's booking page: the text reply gives the page and sends nothing, and only the page's tap sends a code (A3-43: 'In a text or chat, the reply gives the page and sends nothing yet. Only the page's tap sends a code'); this is that tap, on the booking page's 'a booking I already have' entry (README default 28). Served by K-09 v1.1 checkBookingFirst (caller.kind page, personId null), after the live check (README default 37) and with the name swapped first (README default 39): if one booking at this business matches the name and the day, a K-22 v1 link_record code goes to its contact on file, their way, never back to the page (K-09 v1.1 default 45), at most one live code per contact (default 51); from a page the send waits for CQ-44 (K-09 v1.1 open gap 51; open gap 25). checkBookingFirst gives the page server only its attempt id, never the code's id, so no typed code can be checked yet (open gap 34; bookingCheckCode). Who may call: anyone with the booking page. Binds: the business from the code, it and the code's kind both live (publicPage); the call acts for no one until the code is right (K-22 v1 rule 4). Changes: a code row and its send only when a booking matches; no booking or record changes ('Nothing changes until you type the code'). Reads: the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe: page.requestId with the device token is the key; a repeat sends no second code and answers the same checkId (K-09 v1.1 checkBookingFirst repeated). Time budget: a code lives 10 minutes (RULES 6.2).

deviceToken.description: The browser's device cookie (opaqueToken): the server keeps its sha256 with the check, so only this browser can type its code (bookingCheckCode).

nameTyped.description: The name the booking is under, as typed (A3-43: 'Ask which booking by name and day. Never read one out'; K-09 v1.1 checkBookingFirst.nameTyped), with any card number or Social Security number in it swapped for its tag first (pageWordsSwap; README default 39).

dayTyped.description: The day, in the business's zone (K-09 v1.1 checkBookingFirst.dayTyped; CQ-05).

bookingCheckStart.response.title: BookingCheckStarted
bookingCheckStart.response.description: The same answer whether or not a booking matched, and nothing about a visit (A3-43: 'These replies use the same words whether or not a booking exists'; 'Never: say anything about a visit, or that one exists, before the check passes'). The page says: 'If that matches a booking, a code goes to the contact on file, their way. Nothing changes until you type the code.'

checkId.description: An opaque id the server makes for this check, never K-09's attempt id, which stays on the server with it (and, once a K-09 minor version gives them, the code's id, its expiry and its person: open gap 34; K-22 v1 rule 4; K-09 v1.1 open gap 29); at least 128 bits from a cryptographically secure random generator (v1 default 18), bound to the device token's sha256 (README default 29). The same whether or not a code went.

expiresAt.description: 10 minutes after the tap, whether or not a code went (RULES 6.2), so the time tells nothing either.

bookingCheckStart.errors.title: BookingCheckStartErrors
bookingCheckStart.errors.description: Nothing was sent; none of them tells whether a booking exists.

bookingCheckStart.exchange.title: BookingCheckStartExchange
bookingCheckStart.exchange.description: One bookingCheckStart request with its outcome.

bookingCheckCode.request.title: BookingCheckCodeRequest
bookingCheckCode.request.description: The code typed back on the booking page (A3-43, B3-35: 'Nothing changes until you type the code'; FS line 701: a request counts 'after a code to that contact is typed back in the same conversation'). To be served by K-09 v1 proveCode, by the K-22 code id the server keeps with the check (K-22 v1 check_proof_code), never one the page sends; but K-09 v1.1 checkBookingFirst gives the page server no code id (its answer is result, attemptId and repeated) and proveCode needs one (tool-api.v1 proveCode.request: proofCodeId), so until a K-09 minor version gives the page server the code id, or none, and its expiry with the attempt, or adds a proveCode by attempt (open gap 34; the action-layer engineer's FAIL 1 on dc9295e), the page entry can check no typed code and never answers checked: it fails closed. A code that does not match takes the no-match path: the page entry answers wrong itself and counts the try, then paused after the fifth, and expired after the 10 minutes (README default 29), which tells no one whether a booking matched. What a right code answers waits for that K-09 minor version, and no v1.1 fixture shows it. Who may call: the browser that tapped (the same device token); any other answers checkNotFound. Binds: no person until the code is right (K-22 v1 rule 4); then the code's person, kept on the server with the check. Changes: the tries the page entry counts (and, once proveCode serves it, the code's use and its tries in K-22 v1 proof_codes); no booking or record. What a passed check then opens on the page, the steps before the visit, is K-21's journey 7 version (v1.5; open gap 26). Reads: the primary, uncached. Repeat: keyed: page.requestId with the check and the device; each new request with a code counts a try. Time budget: 10 minutes; 5 wrong give a 15-minute pause (RULES 6.2).

code.description: The code as typed (digits; K-22 v1 keeps only its keyed hash, never the code). It never enters a span, a log or the event log.

deviceToken.description: The same device cookie the check started with.

bookingCheckCode.response.title: BookingCheckCodeResponse
bookingCheckCode.response.description: Where the check stands (K-22 v1 check_proof_code's outcomes, as K-09 v1 proveCode gives them). Until a K-09 minor version gives the page server the code id, the page entry gives them itself and never checked: wrong, paused and expired for a code that does not match (open gap 34; README default 29).

oneOf.title: BookingCheckPassed
oneOf.description: The code was right: the check passed (S13-45's one rule; K-09 v1 proveCode right), and the server keeps the code's person with the check. No call answers it until a K-09 minor version gives the page server the code id (open gap 34), so v1.1 has no fixture of it; the shape stays so the page is built for it. The page says only that the check passed; the booking itself and its change or cancel are the steps before the visit (A3-43: 'Goes on as the steps before the visit, once the check passes'), K-21's journey 7 version (v1.5), which takes the check by its checkId with the same device token (open gap 26).

oneOf.title: BookingCheckWrong
oneOf.description: A code that does not match: a wrong code, or any code when no booking matched: one of 5 tries (RULES 6.2; K-09 v1 proveCode wrong), counted per business, name typed and day typed, the key a live code has (README default 29). What a right code answers before open gap 34's K-09 minor version is left to that version.

oneOf.title: BookingCheckPaused
oneOf.description: The fifth wrong code paused the check for 15 minutes (RULES 6.2); the page sends no further code until then.

oneOf.title: BookingCheckExpired
oneOf.description: Past the code's 10 minutes (RULES 6.2), whether or not a code went; the page taps again.

anyOf.title: CheckNotFoundError
anyOf.description: No check with this id was started by this device, or its business no longer matches the code: one answer, so another browser learns nothing.

bookingCheckCode.exchange.title: BookingCheckCodeExchange
bookingCheckCode.exchange.description: One bookingCheckCode request with its outcome.
